instruction: Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_021_three_plate_assembly.step containing base_plate, spacer, and top_plate. Keep all three as independent parts. Move the spacer to the center on top of base_plate, then place top_plate on top of the spacer so the stack is vertical and all XY centers align. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_021_stack_assembly_out.step and write C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_021_massprops.txt containing assembly mass or volume properties.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_022_hole_transfer.step with source_plate and target_plate. Detect all six 6 mm through-hole centers on source_plate. Project/copy the same relative XY hole locations to target_plate and cut six 6 mm through holes in target_plate. Do not modify source_plate. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_022_hole_transfer_out.step with both plates retained.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_023_cutter_boolean_plate.step containing main_plate and twelve cutter_cylinder bodies. Use all cutter cylinders as Boolean subtract tools to cut twelve 5 mm through holes in main_plate. Delete all cutter cylinders after the cut so only the machined main_plate remains. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_023_cut_plate_out.step as one solid.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_024_batch_scale_parts.step containing bracket_A, bracket_B, and bracket_C. Scale only bracket_B uniformly by factor 1.25 while preserving its local origin position. Do not change bracket_A or bracket_C. Export the complete assembly as C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_024_scaled_assembly_out.step and also export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_024_A.step, C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_024_B_scaled.step, and C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_024_C.step as separate part STEP files.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_025_import_repair_shell.step, an imported shell model with small gaps and duplicate faces. Run Import Diagnostics or equivalent repair to close gaps, remove duplicate faces, and stitch it into a closed solid without changing the outer size by more than 0.2 mm. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_025_repaired_solid_out.step and write C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_025_repair_log.txt describing the repair actions.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_026_interference_assembly.step containing housing and sliding_pin. Move sliding_pin along its own axis until there is no solid interference and the minimum axial clearance to housing is 0.5 mm. Do not resize either part. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_026_clearance_fixed_out.step and write C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_026_interference_report.txt indicating zero interference.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_027_mass_target_bracket.step. Without changing the outer bounding box, add evenly distributed through lightening holes in the main plate until the theoretical aluminum mass at density 2.70 g/cm3 is 180 +/- 2 g. All new holes must pass through the main plate, have diameters between 6 and 12 mm, and must not cut through the reinforcing rib. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_027_mass_reduced_out.step and C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_027_massprops.txt.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_028_small_hole_cleanup.step, a 180 x 120 x 6 mm panel containing eighteen round holes. Fill or delete all ten through holes whose diameter is smaller than 3 mm. Preserve all eight functional through holes whose diameter is at least 6 mm, including their positions. Keep the panel outside shape and thickness unchanged. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_028_cleanup_out.step and C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_028_cleanup_report.txt stating that ten small holes were removed.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_029_variant_base_plate.step, a 140 x 70 x 8 mm base plate with a 20 mm center hole. Generate three variants from the same input: S has four 6 mm bolt holes on radius 30 mm, M has six 6 mm bolt holes on radius 38 mm, and L has eight 8 mm bolt holes on radius 46 mm. Keep the center hole and outer shape unchanged. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_029_variant_S.step, C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_029_variant_M.step, and C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_029_variant_L.step.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_030_split_multibody.step containing five separated unnamed bodies: base, left_cover, right_cover, pin, and washer. Identify them by geometry and position. Export each body separately as C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_030_base.step, C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_030_left_cover.step, C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_030_right_cover.step, C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_030_pin.step, and C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_030_washer.step. Also export the unchanged full assembly as C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_030_full_assembly_out.step. Do not change any size or position.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_031_ribbed_enclosure.step, an open enclosure base of outer size 110 x 75 x 22 mm. Add a grid of internal bottom ribs: three ribs along X and two ribs along Y. Each rib is 2.5 mm wide and 6 mm high, and each rib end remains 4 mm away from the inner wall. Merge the ribs into the same solid as the enclosure. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_031_ribbed_enclosure_out.step while preserving the outer bounding box.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_032_draft_wall_part.step, an 80 x 50 x 35 mm open box with vertical outer side walls. Apply a 2 degree outward draft to all four outer side walls using the bottom face as the neutral plane. Keep the bottom size 80 x 50 mm fixed and do not move the bottom. The top size should increase consistently with 35 mm height and 2 degree draft. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_032_drafted_part_out.step.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_033_mirror_pair_right.step, a right-hand bracket fully in X>0. Create a left-hand mirrored version using the YZ plane as the mirror plane while leaving the original right-hand part unchanged. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_033_right_original.step, C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_033_left_mirrored.step, and an assembly C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_033_pair_assembly.step containing both parts with 20 mm minimum spacing in X and no interference.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_034_pin_array_fixture.step containing fixture_plate and ten loose_pin parts. Insert each loose pin into one locating hole in the fixture plate so every pin axis is coaxial with its hole axis and each pin bottom is flush with the hole bottom. Do not scale pins. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_034_pins_inserted_out.step as an assembly retaining eleven solids or components.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_035_flat_pattern_bracket.step, a 2 mm thick U-shaped sheet metal bracket with outside width 60 mm, side height 35 mm, and bottom width 40 mm. Generate a flat pattern using bend inside radius 2 mm and K-factor 0.5. Export the unfolded 2 mm thick flat sheet as C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_035_flat_pattern_out.step and also export the original bent part as C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_035_bent_original.step.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_036_mold_split_simple.step, a drafted plastic housing from Z=0 to Z=40 with maximum section near Z=20. Split the part at the Z=20 mm parting plane into core_side and cavity_side solids. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_036_core_side.step and C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_036_cavity_side.step. The two solids must not overlap, their split faces must lie on Z=20, and their Boolean union must equal the original geometry.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_037_replace_component_assembly.step and C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_037_new_motor.step. Remove old_motor from the assembly and insert the new motor. Align the new motor mounting holes to the frame holes and align the new motor shaft axis coaxially with the coupler. Preserve frame and coupler geometry and avoid new interference. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_037_replaced_motor_out.step containing frame, new_motor, and coupler only.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_038_bounding_box_normalize.step containing eight randomly oriented bracket parts. For each part, apply only rigid rotation and translation so its mounting face points toward -Z and its longest axis points toward +X. Arrange the eight parts on a 4 x 2 grid with X spacing 120 mm and Y spacing 90 mm. Do not change any part dimensions. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_038_normalized_layout_out.step.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_039_threaded_insert_geometry.step, a cylindrical insert blank of outside diameter 16 mm, length 24 mm, and 6 mm through center hole. Create visible simplified external thread geometry over the middle 18 mm length with thread outside diameter 16 mm, root diameter 14.4 mm, and pitch 2 mm. Leave 3 mm unthreaded lead-in sections at both ends and keep the 6 mm bore through. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_039_threaded_insert_out.step.

Using SolidWorks command-line automation, open C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_040_step_quality_export.step, a six-part mechanical assembly. Do not change the geometry. Perform a standardized export to STEP AP242 in millimeters while preserving assembly structure and colors. Also generate C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_040_quality_report.txt listing solid or part count, each part bounding box, and the total assembly bounding box. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\cli_040_ap242_quality_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_001_mounting_plate.step in SolidWorks. The input is one 120 x 80 x 10 mm mounting plate centered at the origin with thickness along Z. Add four fully through round holes on the top face at centers (45,25), (45,-25), (-45,25), and (-45,-25), each with diameter 8 mm. Add 2 mm chamfers to the eight outside perimeter edges. Keep the plate center, thickness, and scale unchanged. Save the modified single-body part as C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_001_mounting_plate_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_002_flange_blank.step, a circular flange blank with outside diameter 100 mm, thickness 12 mm, and Z-axis center. Cut one through center bore of diameter 40 mm. Add six equally spaced through bolt holes of diameter 7 mm on a bolt circle radius of 35 mm, with the first hole on +X. Add 1.5 mm fillets to the upper and lower outside circular edges. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_002_flange_out.step as one part in millimeters with the center at the origin.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_003_shaft.step, a stepped shaft along X with a 30 mm diameter left segment 60 mm long and a 22 mm diameter right segment 50 mm long. On the 30 mm segment, cut a top keyway open toward +Z, width 8 mm, depth 3 mm, length 35 mm, centered at X=20 and centered along the shaft. Add 1 mm chamfers to the two shaft end edges. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_003_shaft_keyway_out.step as a single solid with the axis still along X.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_004_electronics_cover.step, a closed 100 x 70 x 18 mm plastic cover. Convert it to a downward-opening thin shell with 2 mm wall thickness. On the top face, cut eight through ventilation slots, each 40 x 3 mm, centered on X=0 and equally spaced in Y from -24 to +24. Add 3 mm fillets to the four inside corners. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_004_cover_vented_out.step while preserving the 100 x 70 x 18 mm outer size.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_005_heat_sink_base.step, a 90 x 50 x 6 mm flat heat-sink base. Add nine parallel fins on the top face. Each fin runs along Y for the full 50 mm length, is 2 mm thick in X, 18 mm high, and the nine fin centers are equally spaced along X with the outermost centers at X=+/-32 mm. Merge fins and base into one connected body. Add 0.5 mm fillets to the fin top edges. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_005_heat_sink_out.step with total height 24 mm.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_006_bracket_L.step, an L bracket with an 80 x 50 x 8 mm base plate and an 80 x 8 x 60 mm vertical plate. Add two through mounting holes in the base, diameter 9 mm, centered at X=+/-25 and Y=0. Add one horizontal obround slot through the vertical plate, total length 32 mm, width 10 mm, centered at X=0 and Z=35. Add two symmetric triangular gussets, each 6 mm thick with 35 mm right-angle legs. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_006_bracket_reinforced_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_007_pipe_elbow.step, a 90 degree pipe elbow with outer diameter 30 mm, inner diameter 20 mm, centerline radius 45 mm, and flat ends. Add one circular flange to each pipe end. Each flange must have outside diameter 58 mm, thickness 8 mm, a center hole matching the 20 mm pipe inner diameter, and four equally spaced through bolt holes of diameter 6 mm on radius 22 mm. The flanges must be coaxial with the elbow ends. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_007_elbow_flanges_out.step as either a single multi-body STEP or an assembly STEP.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_008_sensor_mount.step, a 60 x 40 x 20 mm sensor mount with a 30 x 20 mm top rectangular recess that is initially 2 mm deep. Deepen the recess to 5 mm, add R3 fillets to its four corners, and cut a centered through cable hole of diameter 12 mm through the recess. Add 1 mm chamfers to the four bottom outside corners. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_008_sensor_mount_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_009_hinge_leaf.step, a hinge leaf with a 90 x 32 x 3 mm flat plate and three existing hinge knuckles along one long edge. Add four countersunk mounting holes on the leaf plate at X=-33, -11, 11, and 33 with Y=0. Each hole has a 4.5 mm through diameter, 8.5 mm countersink top diameter, and 90 degree countersink angle. Also adjust the hinge pin bore through all knuckles to diameter 4.2 mm. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_009_hinge_leaf_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_010_wheel_blank.step, a wheel disk blank with outside diameter 120 mm, thickness 20 mm, and Z-axis center. Cut a 35 mm diameter through center hole. Add five through bolt holes of diameter 9 mm on radius 42 mm, with the first hole on +Y and angular spacing 72 degrees. Add 2 mm fillets to both outside circular rim edges. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_010_wheel_pattern_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_011_nozzle_blank.step, a cylindrical nozzle blank of outside diameter 36 mm, total length 70 mm along Z, with an existing 10 mm through center bore. Machine the upper half into a 15 degree external taper over 35 mm length, ending at top outside diameter 18 mm and smoothly meeting the original 36 mm diameter. Add a bottom flange of outside diameter 60 mm and thickness 8 mm. Add four through bolt holes of diameter 6 mm on flange hole radius 23 mm. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_011_nozzle_flanged_out.step with the nozzle axis on Z.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_012_pcb_support_plate.step, a 100 x 60 x 4 mm flat PCB support plate. Add four cylindrical standoffs at (35,20), (35,-20), (-35,20), and (-35,-20). Each standoff has diameter 8 mm and height 12 mm. Cut a 3.2 mm diameter M3 clearance through hole through each standoff and the base plate. Add 6 mm corner fillets to the plate corners. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_012_pcb_support_out.step with total height 16 mm.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_013_clamp_jaw.step, an 80 x 30 x 25 mm clamp jaw block. On the clamping face, cut a V groove that runs the full length along X, has included angle 90 degrees, and depth 8 mm. Add two M6 mounting through holes from the top, using geometric diameter 6.5 mm, centered at X=+/-25 and Y=0. Add 1 mm fillets to all outside edges. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_013_clamp_vjaw_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_014_handle_blank.step, a handle blank with two cylindrical end bosses of diameter 18 mm and height 8 mm, center distance 64 mm, connected by a rectangular bridge. Remodel the bridge so its upper surface has an ergonomic arc transition with radius 10 mm and the highest point is 12 mm above the end-boss top face. Cut a 5 mm through mounting hole at the center of each end boss. Add 0.8 mm fillets to all exposed outside edges. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_014_handle_ergonomic_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_015_gear_blank.step, an 80 mm diameter, 10 mm thick gear disk blank with an existing 12 mm center hole. Do not create real involute teeth. Instead cut six through sector-shaped lightening windows, equally spaced. Each window lies between radii 22 mm and 32 mm and has angular width 24 degrees. Keep the 12 mm center hole and preserve the 80 mm outside diameter and 10 mm thickness. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_015_gear_lightened_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_016_frame_corner.step, a 90 degree frame corner made from two 30 x 30 x 120 mm square tubes with 3 mm wall thickness. Add one diagonal gusset plate in the inside corner connecting the inner faces of the tubes. The gusset plate thickness is 6 mm and its projected right-angle legs are each 55 mm. Near the outside end of each tube, add two 8 mm diameter through fixing holes with hole centers 20 mm from the tube end face and 16 mm hole spacing. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_016_frame_corner_gusset_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_017_adapter_block.step, a 70 x 50 x 18 mm adapter block with a 20 mm through center hole. Enlarge the center hole to diameter 25 mm. Add four counterbored holes at (25,15), (25,-15), (-25,15), and (-25,-15). Each counterbored hole has 6 mm through diameter, 12 mm counterbore diameter, and 5 mm counterbore depth from the top face. Add a 2 mm chamfer to the top outer perimeter. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_017_adapter_counterbore_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_018_motor_mount.step, a motor mount with a 100 x 80 x 8 mm base plate and a centered top boss of diameter 50 mm and height 12 mm. Cut a 22 mm through center hole through the boss. Add four motor mounting holes of diameter 5.5 mm on radius 32 mm at angles 45, 135, 225, and 315 degrees. Add two obround base mounting slots, each total length 24 mm and width 8 mm, centered at X=+/-35 and Y=0. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_018_motor_mount_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_019_cover_with_bosses.step, a thin cover of size 120 x 90 x 5 mm with R8 outside corners and four top cylindrical bosses of diameter 10 mm and height 10 mm. Convert each boss into a screw post by cutting a 3.4 mm diameter through hole through the boss and the cover. Add four reinforcing ribs between adjacent bosses; each rib is 4 mm wide, 6 mm high, and runs along a straight line near the boss outside diameters. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_019_cover_boss_ribs_out.step.

Open C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_020_two_part_alignment.step, a STEP assembly with base_block and sliding_block. The base block is 100 x 40 x 10 mm and the sliding block is 30 x 30 x 12 mm. Move the sliding_block to the center of the base_block top face so the sliding_block bottom face touches the base_block top face and their XY centers coincide. Do not change either part size. Export C:\Users\User\Desktop\gui_020_two_part_aligned_out.step as an assembly or multi-body STEP retaining two independent solids.
